summary: Reviewed ModuleJsonExportGenerator at src/classes/Application/Composer/ModulesOverview/ModuleJsonExportGenerator.php against all four review dimensions. No blocking issues found.

Maintainability: Class is well-structured, concise, and fully documented. Method decomposition is appropriate (generate() orchestrates; private buildGlossary() and collectGlossarySections() are cleanly extracted). The protected hook methods use the Template Method pattern correctly.

Best Practices: Consistent with the established ModulesOverview module patterns. array() syntax used throughout. No constructor promotion. No final modifier on the generator class (required for subclassability). SOLID principles observed — single responsibility, open/closed via hooks.

Path handling: Verified that the rtrim() calls on $sourcePath in both generate() and resolveModuleBrief() are necessary, not redundant — ModuleInfoParser::resolveSourcePath() returns paths with a trailing slash (e.g. 'assets/classes/Variables/'). The defensive rtrim in the protected hook is correct because the parameter comes from an external caller.
Performance: No bottlenecks. The $includeAll filter correctly skips README parsing and source resolution for modules without a brief, avoiding wasted I/O.

Future context: The two-hook design (resolveModuleSource + resolveModuleBrief) is a clean, minimal extension surface for subclasses. The HCP Editor thin subclass (WP-007) can override both without touching the core orchestration loop.

comments.note: No blocking issues found — code is clean, well-structured, and consistent with the established patterns in the ModulesOverview module.

The rtrim() calls on $sourcePath inside generate() (for the README path) and inside resolveModuleBrief() are both necessary: ModuleInfoParser::resolveSourcePath() appends a trailing slash to all returned relative paths, so $module->getSourcePath() always ends with '/'. The defensive stripping in the protected hook is correct for a method that accepts a caller-supplied path parameter.
